text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Semiconductor equipment supplier ASM International and electronic publisher AND make their Amsterdam bourse debut. (p1)
- Dutch consumer association calls for European ban on genetically modified corn. (p1)
- EMU stability pact still uncertain. (p1)
- Ministry of Economic Affairs to act as guarantor for credits to small firms doing business with eastern Europe. (p3)
- Belgian steel group Boel, which is to be taken over by steel maker Hoogovens, wants to shed 787 out of 2,000 jobs. (p3)
- Transport companies Van Ommeren and Pakhoed team up in project for port storage terminal in China. (p3)
- Royal Dutch/Shell's U.S. unit Shell Oil to invest $10 bln in oil and gas fields in Gulf of Mexico. (p4)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Prime Minister Wim Kok criticises French president Jacques Chirac's "bossy tone" in debate on drugs policy. (p1)
- 12 Dutch first division soccer clubs will meet on Saturday to discuss creation of a "super league" system. (p1)
- Finance minister Gerrit Zalm wants investigation into possibility of Dutch gold being held in Swiss bank vaults. (p3)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Broadcasting organisation VARA ordered to pay eight million guilders in damages to former soft drinks producer for allegations made in a programme 25 years ago. (p7)
- Tough parking regulations keep tourists away from the Netherlands, according to Dutch tourist office NBT. (p9)
- Dutch banks do not want to be obliged to inform the government of dividends paid to their clients. (p25)
- Textile firm Gamma takes 50 pct stake in Fench car textile maker Delcar. (p27)
TROUW
- Beverages maker Bols is considering bringing back part of its spirits production to the Netherlands. (6)
- Government gives 194 million guilders to NS Cargo to enable the state-owned rail company to make investments. (p7)
-- Amsterdam newsdesk +31 20 504 5000
